security_audit.summary: The review confirms critical remote curl-to-shell installation instructions and a dangerous mix of command execution, credentials, and network access. Additional risks include shell injection, incomplete SSRF controls, account-linked telemetry, global cross-project data exposure, automatic dependency installation, nested Codex prompting, and unenforced paid-provider consent. Many scanner matches are harmless tests, documentation, template strings, or fixed argv execution, but binary blind spots and capped static coverage still require manual review. Static review was capped at 400/1557 representative findings; omitted static matches are unconfirmed, so automatic publishing stays disabled until manual review.

remediation.suggestion: Manually review the omitted 1157 static analyzer matches or reduce bundled generated/vendor/reference content before enabling automatic publication.

remediation.issue: Remote installer is piped directly into bash.
remediation.suggestion: Publish versioned artifacts with checksums or signatures. Download, verify, and execute a pinned installer as separate steps.

remediation.issue: Local model commands use shell:true with interpolated values.
remediation.suggestion: Tokenize fixed command templates and call execFile or spawn with an argv array. Validate every path, prompt, and numeric parameter.

remediation.issue: Direct URL validation checks only literal hostnames.
remediation.suggestion: Resolve DNS before connection, reject private and metadata addresses, disable or validate redirects, and recheck every resolved destination.

remediation.issue: Telemetry links events to email or username by default.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit consent before account identification. Use a random identifier by default and document retention, destination, and deletion controls.

remediation.issue: Global caching stores project assets and prompt metadata automatically.
remediation.suggestion: Make cross-project promotion opt-in, isolate caches by workspace, redact prompt and client metadata, and add cache inspection and deletion commands.

remediation.issue: Untrusted intent is forwarded to an authenticated Codex sub-agent.
remediation.suggestion: Use strict prompt delimiters, validate intent, restrict the subprocess environment and permissions, and require explicit provider approval before execution.

remediation.issue: BGM generation installs unpinned Python packages automatically.
remediation.suggestion: Remove runtime installation. Provide a locked dependency file, require explicit setup, and verify package hashes in an isolated environment.

remediation.issue: The paid provider flag is informational only.
remediation.suggestion: Enforce a confirmation token or explicit provider selection before any provider marked paid can run.

remediation.issue: Binary assets and lower-priority static matches remain unreviewed.
remediation.suggestion: Inspect every binary asset, verify provenance and hashes, and complete review of the 1,157 static matches omitted by the reporting cap.

semantic_findings.title: Account-Linked Telemetry Sends Personal Identifiers
semantic_findings.description: Telemetry reads the signed-in HeyGen email or username and sends it to PostHog as a distinct identifier. Collection is enabled by default and requires an environment opt-out.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The code directly reads user.email or user.username from the credential file and posts an identify event to PostHog.

semantic_findings.title: Global Cache Exposes Assets and Prompts Across Projects
semantic_findings.description: Resolved files and complete manifest records are copied into a global cache. Candidate listing returns descriptions and prompt text from unrelated projects, including other client work.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The documentation explicitly warns that another client's brand mark and prompt can surface, and the code stores and returns those fields.

semantic_findings.title: Untrusted Intent Is Delegated to an Authenticated Codex Agent
semantic_findings.description: Media intent is concatenated directly into a Codex execution prompt without delimiters. On image fallback, the nested agent runs automatically and is instructed not to request confirmation.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The code directly embeds intent before imperative instructions and launches codex exec with authenticated image tooling during the normal fallback cascade.

semantic_findings.title: Unpinned Python Dependencies Install Without Approval
semantic_findings.description: Missing BGM dependencies trigger python -m pip install automatically. Package versions are not pinned, and installation occurs before local music generation without user confirmation.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The implementation explicitly invokes pip install for unversioned dependency arrays when import probes fail.

semantic_findings.title: Direct URL SSRF Guard Can Be Bypassed
semantic_findings.description: The direct URL validator blocks only literal private hostnames. DNS rebinding, private DNS resolution, and redirects can bypass the check before the URL is fetched.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The source comment acknowledges the DNS resolution gap, and fetch follows validation without resolving or rechecking the destination.

semantic_findings.title: Paid Provider Confirmation Is Not Enforced
semantic_findings.description: HeyGen TTS is marked as potentially paid, but provider dispatch ignores the paid flag. A normal voice request can invoke billable service after free quota is exhausted.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The registry documents confirmation as required and marks HeyGen TTS paid, while runProviders invokes the capability without checking consent.

critical_findings.title: Pipe to shell pattern
critical_findings.confidence_reasoning: The exported installation command downloads a remote script and pipes it directly to bash without pinning or verification. A compromised host or script can execute arbitrary code.

critical_findings.title: Pipe to shell pattern
critical_findings.confidence_reasoning: The setup instructions tell users to execute a network response directly with bash. There is no checksum, signature, version pin, or inspection step.

critical_findings.title: Pipe to shell pattern

content.value_statement: Media workflows often scatter assets, provider commands, and metadata across many tools. This skill centralizes resolution, generation, processing, caching, and reuse.
actual_capabilities: Resolves music, sound effects, images, icons, logos, voices, grades, and LUTs through ordered provider cascades.
Generates voice, music, and images through HeyGen, local models, or Codex when configured.
Builds voiceover metadata, word timestamps, sound cues, and background music for video workflows.
Ingests local files or direct public media URLs into a project manifest.
Caches resolved assets and lists reusable candidates across projects.
Analyzes media with ffmpeg and produces color grading suggestions or validated LUT files.
limitations: Many features require external CLIs, ffmpeg, provider credentials, or downloaded local models.
Network providers, telemetry, and cross-project caching require careful privacy review.
Automatic provider fallback can invoke authenticated services when local or catalog results are unavailable.
The skill does not replace human review for brand accuracy, media rights, or final creative quality.

use_cases.title: Assemble Video Assets
use_cases.description: Resolve voiceover, background music, sound effects, images, and grades for a structured video project.

use_cases.title: Automate Media Pipelines
use_cases.description: Create repeatable asset resolution, ingestion, manifests, captions, and media processing steps.

use_cases.title: Reuse Approved Brand Media
use_cases.description: Find prior logos, images, music, and visual treatments before requesting new provider assets.

prompt_templates.title: Resolve One Asset
prompt_templates.prompt: Resolve a {media type} for {project}. The intent is {description}. Prefer an existing project asset before using a provider.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for one media asset

prompt_templates.title: Build an Audio Pass
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an audio plan for {project} using this narration: {script}. Include voice, background music, sound cues, and caption timing.

prompt_templates.title: Review Reuse Candidates
prompt_templates.prompt: List reusable {media type} candidates for {intent}. Compare project and global results, then recommend only exact or clearly suitable matches.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Full Media Pipeline
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan and execute media resolution for {project}. Use local-only mode where possible, require approval before external services, and document every output.

output_examples.input: Resolve upbeat launch music for a product video.
output_examples.output: Resolved a reusable background track, copied it into the project media folder, and recorded its duration and provider.

output_examples.input: Create voiceover and captions from a three-scene script.
output: Generated one voice file per scene.
Recorded word timings for caption authoring.
Reported total narration duration and any failed lines.

output_examples.input: Apply a warm cinematic grade to a local frame.
output_examples.output: Analyzed the frame, returned bounded exposure and color suggestions, and identified a matching local grade preset.

best_practices: Run dependency checks before resolving assets and review every requested external provider.
Use local-only mode for sensitive projects and keep provider credentials scoped to the task.
Review global cache candidates carefully before reusing brand or client-specific assets.
anti_patterns: Do not pipe remote installation scripts directly into a shell.
Do not reuse cross-project assets from a loose prompt or brand match.
Do not allow untrusted text to control shell commands or nested agent prompts.

faq.question: What media types can this skill manage?
faq.answer: It supports background music, sound effects, images, icons, logos, voices, color grades, LUTs, captions, and related media operations.

faq.question: Does it work without network access?
faq.answer: Local-only mode skips network providers. Results then depend on project assets, the global cache, and installed local tools.

faq.question: Which credentials can it use?
faq.answer: It can use HeyGen, ElevenLabs, Google, Gemini, Codex, and related CLI authentication when those providers are selected.

faq.question: Does it send telemetry?
faq.answer: Yes. It sends usage events by default and can link them to a signed-in HeyGen account. Environment variables disable telemetry.

faq.question: How does cross-project reuse work?
faq.answer: Resolved assets and metadata can enter a global home-directory cache. Candidate listing can surface those records in later projects.

faq.question: Does it guarantee media rights or brand accuracy?
faq.answer: No. Users must verify licenses, ownership, brand correctness, provider terms, and final creative suitability.
